The improvements in survival of gynaecological cancer in the Anglia region of England, as reported by the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, appear to be largely due to the adoption of a multifaceted approach to care, including centralisation of surgery and use of multidisciplinary management. This integrated approach has resulted in significant improvements in patient outcomes.

The 1999 guidance on gynaecological cancer, which included multidisciplinary case management and centralisation of surgery, played a crucial role in this improvement. This guidance encouraged the integration of various healthcare specialties, leading to better coordination and communication among healthcare professionals.

Furthermore, the establishment of multidisciplinary breast cancer clinics has also contributed to these improvements. These clinics provide comprehensive care by involving specialists from different fields, which has helped in improving patient outcomes.

The improved survival rates for patients with gynaecological cancer in the Anglia region can be attributed to several factors:

1. Centralisation of surgery: This allowed for better planning and execution of complex surgeries, which is essential for gynaecological cancer.
2. Multidisciplinary management: The involvement of various healthcare professionals has improved patient outcomes by providing a comprehensive approach to care.
3. Integration of specialist care: The incorporation of specialists from different fields has enhanced the quality of care provided, leading to better patient outcomes.

In conclusion, the improvements in survival rates for gynaecological cancer patients in the Anglia region can be attributed to the effective adoption of multidisciplinary management and centralisation of care, which have resulted in improved coordination and communication among healthcare professionals.
